concepts.def: Temperature range 5-63 °C where bacteria multiply rapidly.
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points — food safety framework.
Critical Control Point — step where hazards can be controlled.
Boundary between safe and unsafe at a CCP (e.g. core temp 75 °C).
FAO/WHO joint food standards body, established 1963.
Time for a bacterial population to double.

walkthroughs.body_html: The danger zone is 5-63 °C. Many pathogens double every 20-30 minutes at body temperature. Cold storage below 5 °C and hot holding above 63 °C suppress growth.
HACCP was developed in the 1960s by Pillsbury, NASA and the US Army for astronaut food. Codified internationally by Codex in 1993, it underpins modern food safety legislation worldwide.
The 7 HACCP principles: identify hazards, identify CCPs, set critical limits, monitor, set corrective actions, verify, document. UK Food Safety regulations require an HACCP-based system.
